column2: Summary
column5: Description

column2: P1-A Foundations & app skeleton
column5: Xcode project, Packages/, design tokens wired in, the macOS CI job switched on, and the one open design decision from Phase 0 settled. Nothing else can start until this does. Refs: PRODUCT.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml, design/generated/DesignTokens.generated.swift

column2: P1-B Data layer, schema & RLS
column5: Supabase migration 001 with RLS on from the first line, SwiftData as the local source of truth, protocol-based repositories, and the outbox. Brief SS04 (core data model) + ADR 0003/0004/0005.

column2: P1-C Authentication
column5: Sign in with Apple via Supabase Auth, plus the Article 9 health-data consent that must be separate from ToS acceptance. Brief SS1.1.

column2: P1-D Pre-Season: onboarding & the SS10 safety gates
column3: P1-D Pre-Season: onboarding & the SS10 safety gates
column5: Onboarding collects only what the engine needs, computes a band via Mifflin-St Jeor, and enforces S1-S7 at build time. docs/safety/safety-requirements.md is the spec; its named tests are the acceptance criteria. Brief SS1.2.

column2: P1-E HealthKit sync
column5: Incremental sync with a persisted anchor, daily buckets via HKStatisticsCollectionQuery, background delivery. The two Phase 0 findings bind this epic and are not negotiable. Brief SS1.4 + docs/phase-0/07-spike-findings.md.

column2: P1-F Sub On: food logging, four routes
column3: P1-F Sub On: food logging, four routes
column5: Manual, text search, barcode, photo. Barcode ships before photo (cheapest, fastest path). The photo route never silently accepts an estimate. Brief SS1.3 + design/redesign/SubOn.dc.html + Var.dc.html.

column2: P1-G The Run: weight & trend
column5: Manual entry plus HealthKit reads, rendered as a 7-day EWMA against the pace chosen at onboarding. Never raw daily weight. Brief SS1.5 + design/redesign/Season.dc.html.

column2: P1-H Matchday: the Today dashboard
column5: One screen: band and remaining, macro split, weight sparkline, Form ring, and a placeholder where the division badge lands in Phase 2. Three tabs maximum across the whole app. Brief SS1.6 + design/redesign/Main.dc.html.

column2: P1-I Offline-first sync
column5: The UI never waits on the network. Outbox drains on reconnect, last-write-wins on server timestamps, verified in airplane mode. ADR 0005.

column2: P1-J Dogfood: 21 consecutive days
column5: The actual purpose of the phase. 21 consecutive days of real logged data on a real device, and the photo-accuracy benchmark that accumulates alongside it. This epic is wall-clock bound - it cannot be compressed by working harder.

column2: P1-X Phase 1 exit criteria
column5: The six testable conditions that close the phase. Phases end on a condition, not a date. Mirror of docs/phase-0/README.md's format.

column2: DECIDE: fixed type scale vs Dynamic Type (ADR 0015)
column5:
The one thing a 393x852 artboard could not settle, and Phase 1's first design task (PRODUCT.md, design/redesign/README.md).

The mockups use the fixed scale in ninety.tokens.json because a static frame cannot express Dynamic Type. iOS wants system text styles and bans hard-coded point sizes. Whichever wins changes how the type tokens are structured, so this blocks every view ticket.

Acceptance criteria
* A decision, written up as ADR 0015 in docs/decisions/ with a pre-written reversal trigger (see docs/decisions/README.md)
* The index table in docs/decisions/README.md updated. Do not renumber existing ADRs
* If Dynamic Type wins: ninety.tokens.json restructured to emit text styles, generate.py updated, generated Swift + CSS regenerated and committed together
* One screen (Matchday) proven at both the smallest and largest accessibility sizes, or an explicit written note that the fixed scale was chosen and why

column2: Create the Ninety/ Xcode project
column5:
No Ninety/ exists yet; creating it is Phase 1's job (CLAUDE.md).

Acceptance criteria
* iOS 18.0 deployment target (ADR 0002), Xcode 26.6 / Swift 6.3
* Swift 6 strict concurrency on, not warnings-only
* Builds and runs on the physical iPhone, not just the Simulator
* Bundle id and team set against the Apple Developer account approved 2026-08-30
* SwiftLint runs as a build phase against the existing .swiftlint.yml

column2: Wire DesignTokens.generated.swift into the app target
column5:
Colours are generated, never hand-written. Editing the Swift by hand is the failure mode this ticket exists to prevent.

Acceptance criteria
* design/generated/DesignTokens.generated.swift compiles inside the app target
* A deliberate hardcoded Color in a view fails the build via the no_hardcoded_colour rule
* python3 design/tokens/generate.py --check still passes in CI

column2: Scaffold Packages/RankingEngine as a pure Swift package
column5:
Phase 2 owns the maths; Phase 1 owns the boundary. Creating the package now means the SwiftLint purity rules have something to police from day one (ADR 0006).

Acceptance criteria
* Packages/RankingEngine builds as a standalone SPM package with no UI imports, no ambient clock, no randomness
* A deliberate `import SwiftUI` inside it fails lint
* Swift Testing target present, even if it only holds one placeholder test

column2: Switch on the gated macOS CI job
column5:
.github/workflows/ci.yml skips the expensive macOS job until Ninety/ exists. Once it does, the path filter should let it run.

Acceptance criteria
* macOS job builds the app and runs the test target on PRs that touch Swift
* Docs- and design-only commits still skip it (200 real macOS minutes/month is the budget)
* SwiftLint runs in CI at the configured severities

column2: Enable the git hooks and prove the safety lint fires
column5:
git config core.hooksPath .githooks. The hooks are already written; nobody has confirmed they bite.

Acceptance criteria
* Secret and health-data tripwires block a deliberate test commit
* commit-msg rejects a non-conventional message
* A string containing one of the 17 banned phrases fails the build at error severity (S5)

column2: App shell: three tabs, no more
column5:
Brief SS1.6 caps the whole app at three tabs. Matchday / The Run / The Table, with The Table showing the Phase 2 placeholder.

Acceptance criteria
* Navigation shell renders with tokens, in the Matchday world (kit stripes in the masthead)
* Every screen's spine fits 393x852 without scrolling
* The Table tab exists and states plainly that ranking arrives in Phase 2 - no fake data, no lorem

column2: Supabase migration 001: every table, RLS on from the first line
column5:
Brief SS04. Retrofitting RLS onto a live database holding real health data is described in the brief as "a genuinely bad afternoon".

Tables: profiles, foods, food_logs, photo_estimates, weight_logs, health_samples, weekly_scores, sync_outbox - plus friendships and leaderboard_entries, created empty now because nothing writes to them until Phase 4 and retrofitting relationships later is painful.

Acceptance criteria
* All ten tables created in one migration, with the key fields listed in the brief
* weekly_scores carries engine_version - without it every historical score becomes meaningless the first time weights are retuned
* ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on every table in the same migration, no exceptions
* Migration is committed and re-runnable from scratch

column2: RLS policies, tested with two real accounts
column5:
Phase 1 exit criterion: "RLS policies on every table, tested with two accounts."

Acceptance criteria
* Per-table select/insert/update/delete policies keyed on auth.uid()
* Account A cannot read, write or delete any row belonging to account B - proven, not assumed
* The test is repeatable and written down (a SQL script or a test target), not a one-off afternoon in the dashboard
* Storage bucket policies cover meal photos too, not just tables

column2: SwiftData models as the local source of truth
column5:
ADR 0005: SwiftData is the local source of truth and the UI never waits on the network.

Acceptance criteria
* Local models mirror the Postgres schema, including sync_outbox
* Every write path goes local-first and returns immediately
* Migration story for the local store exists (it will change during the 21 days)

column2: Protocol-based repositories with mocks
column5:
ADR 0004. Views -> @Observable ViewModels -> protocol repositories -> SwiftData / Supabase / HealthKit.

Acceptance criteria
* One protocol per data domain: food, weight, health, profile
* Mock implementations injectable in tests; no ViewModel test touches the network, the device or the disk
* Repositories return an empty result rather than throwing when there is no data - the HealthKit finding makes this a rule, not a preference

column2: Mirror Open Food Facts + USDA into Postgres with a tsvector index
column5:
Brief SS1.3, Path 1. Never call a third-party API on every keystroke: slow, rate-limited, fails offline.

Acceptance criteria
* Both sources imported into the foods table with source correctly set (off/usda/custom)
* search_vector populated and GIN-indexed; a two-word query returns in well under 100 ms
* A documented, re-runnable refresh path - this data goes stale
* Sensible subset if the full dump is unwieldy; write down what was cut and why

column2: Sign in with Apple via Supabase Auth
column5:
Brief SS1.1. A paid-programme entitlement, which is now available.

Acceptance criteria
* Sign in, sign out, and session restore across a cold launch
* Supabase session token refreshes without user action
* No third-party login is offered, so no Apple rework is needed later
* Failure states use the copy deck's wording, not raw error strings

column2: Health-data consent, separate from terms acceptance
column5:
UK GDPR Article 9: health data is special category data and needs explicit consent with a documented lawful basis. Required before the first external tester, but the screen belongs in onboarding, so build it now.

Acceptance criteria
* Consent for health data is a distinct, separately-recorded action from accepting terms
* test_health_consent_is_separate_from_terms_acceptance passes
* Consent timestamp persisted on the profile

column2: Pre-Season onboarding flow
column4: P1-D Pre-Season: onboarding & the SS10 safety gates
column5:
design/redesign/screens/1-pre-season.png and Signing.dc.html. Collect only what the scoring engine needs: date of birth, height, sex, activity level, goal type, target rate of change.

Acceptance criteria
* Every field persists to profiles
* Every safety gate is stated in the flow rather than hidden behind a silent validation
* Copy comes from design/spec/04-copy-deck.md SS1, unchanged
* Resumable: quitting mid-flow does not lose what was entered

column2: Mifflin-St Jeor target, presented as a band
column4: P1-D Pre-Season: onboarding & the SS10 safety gates
column5:
"Hitting exactly 1,847 kcal is not a real human goal; landing between 1,750 and 1,950 is." The band is never rendered as two numbers joined by a dash - it is one figure plus a tolerance (612 +/-100), per PRODUCT.md.

Acceptance criteria
* Target computed from DOB, height, sex, activity level and goal
* Rendered as figure plus tolerance everywhere it appears
* Recomputes when the profile changes

column2: S1: hard minimum calorie floor, clamping
column4: P1-D Pre-Season: onboarding & the SS10 safety gates
column5:
Female 1,200 / male 1,500 / unspecified 1,500 kcal per day. Clamp, do not reject - then offer the lever that helps (a slower rate), rather than leaving the user stuck at the floor.

Named tests (acceptance criteria)
* test_calorie_target_never_below_floor_female
* test_calorie_target_never_below_floor_male
* test_unspecified_sex_uses_higher_floor
* test_floor_breach_surfaces_slower_rate_option
* test_floor_applies_after_deficit_not_before

column2: S2: goal weight validated against BMI 18.5, rejecting
column4: P1-D Pre-Season: onboarding & the SS10 safety gates
column5:
minimum acceptable goal weight = 18.5 * height_m^2. Reject, do not clamp - silently substituting a goal would be dishonest about what the app tracks toward. Deliberately asymmetric: no upper bound.

Named tests (acceptance criteria)
* test_goal_weight_below_bmi_18_5_is_rejected
* test_goal_weight_at_bmi_18_5_is_accepted
* test_rejection_states_the_minimum_acceptable_weight
* test_no_upper_bound_on_goal_weight
* test_bmi_uses_metres_not_centimetres

column2: S3: rate-of-loss ceiling enforced in onboarding
column4: P1-D Pre-Season: onboarding & the SS10 safety gates
column5:
ceiling = min(1.0 kg/week, 1% of current body weight per week). Selectable rates 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75, filtered to those at or below the ceiling. There is deliberately no "maximum" option.

The scoring half of S3 - progress score peaking at target rate - is Phase 2 and explicitly out of scope here.

Named tests (acceptance criteria)
* test_rate_ceiling_is_one_percent_bodyweight_for_light_user
* test_rate_ceiling_caps_at_1kg_for_heavy_user
* test_onboarding_hides_rates_above_ceiling

column2: S4: age gate, hard stop, with signposting
column4: P1-D Pre-Season: onboarding & the SS10 safety gates
column5:
Under 18 is a hard stop with no bypass: no "continue anyway", no parental-consent path. Computed on the actual date, not a year subtraction. The rejection screen signposts Beat's youth helpline - a user turned away should not leave with nothing.

Named tests (acceptance criteria)
* test_under_18_is_blocked
* test_exactly_18_today_is_allowed
* test_17_years_364_days_is_blocked
* test_no_bypass_path_exists_from_the_age_gate
* test_age_gate_screen_includes_support_signposting

column2: S5: no punishment framing, enforced in the build
column4: P1-D Pre-Season: onboarding & the SS10 safety gates
column5:
17 banned phrases at lint-error severity, plus the structural half: no error colour for logged intake, a missed day renders empty rather than crossed out, no streak-loss animation, and losing a division always states the way back.

Named tests (acceptance criteria)
* test_no_banned_phrase_in_any_localised_string
* test_missed_day_renders_empty_not_negative
* test_over_band_state_does_not_use_critical_colour
* test_tier_regression_copy_states_the_path_back (copy only in Phase 1; there is no tier yet)

column2: S6: competitive opt-out, two taps from Matchday
column4: P1-D Pre-Season: onboarding & the SS10 safety gates
column5:
A switch that disables every competitive and social feature while leaving a fully useful food and weight tracker. "An opt-out that leaves a crippled app is not an opt-out - it is a threat."

Named tests (acceptance criteria)
* test_opt_out_hides_rank_tab
* test_opt_out_stops_score_computation
* test_opt_out_preserves_food_logging
* test_opt_out_preserves_weight_trend_and_healthkit_sync
* test_opt_out_is_reachable_in_two_taps
* test_opt_out_is_reversible_and_preserves_history

column2: S7: signposting always available in Settings
column4: P1-D Pre-Season: onboarding & the SS10 safety gates
column5:
Beat (0808 801 0677) and the National Alliance for Eating Disorders, permanently in Settings. The pattern-based triggers are a Phase 3 gate and are explicitly out of scope here.

Acceptance criteria
* test_signposting_always_available_in_settings
* test_signposting_copy_contains_no_diagnostic_language
* The "not a medical device" footer appears wherever it fits

column2: Calibration window state: 7 days, no rank shown
column4: P1-D Pre-Season: onboarding & the SS10 safety gates
column5:
ADR 0018: the first 7 days are a calibration window, shown as "CALIBRATING - N days to go", with no rank displayed. The brief said 14; the ADR halved it and records what the thinner baseline costs.

Acceptance criteria
* profiles.calibration_completed_at set and honoured
* The Table tab shows the calibrating state, not an empty leaderboard
* Countdown is correct across a date change and a timezone change

column2: HealthKit entitlement, usage strings and authorisation
column5:
Types: bodyMass, stepCount, activeEnergyBurned, appleExerciseTime, HKWorkoutType.

Acceptance criteria
* Entitlement and Info.plist usage descriptions in place; the sheet appears on first run
* Authorisation requested once, not on every launch
* authorizationStatus(for:) is not used to infer read access anywhere - it reports write permission only, and using it to infer reads is a trap (measured, Spike A)

column2: Daily buckets via HKStatisticsCollectionQuery
column5:
Hard rule from Spike A: never iterate raw samples to build a daily total. Measured ~1,830 step samples and ~3,000 active-energy samples per day; the naive version has the Today screen chewing through ~123,000 objects per launch.

Acceptance criteria
* All daily totals come from HKStatisticsCollectionQuery, bucketed at local midnight
* Cumulative vs discrete mapping is correct - bodyMass is averaged, never summed. Getting this wrong produces plausible nonsense
* No code path enumerates raw samples for a total; a review checklist item or a lint rule enforces it

column2: Anchored sync with the anchor persisted to health_samples
column5:
Brief SS1.4 calls the persisted anchor "the entire trick". Spike A measured it: 56,764 samples on the first read, 0 on the second, and the anchor survived a force-quit.

Acceptance criteria
* HKAnchoredObjectQuery with the anchor stored in health_samples.hk_anchor, not UserDefaults (that was the spike's shortcut)
* result.deletedObjects is handled - it is not optional to handle
* A cold launch after a previous sync reads approximately nothing
* Written against the async descriptor API, not the callback form every tutorial online shows

column2: HKObserverQuery + background delivery
column5:
What the spike deliberately skipped: updates while the app is backgrounded.

Acceptance criteria
* enableBackgroundDelivery(for:frequency:) registered for the read types
* A weight written by a scale while the app is backgrounded appears without a manual refresh
* Background wakeups do not re-read full history

column2: Empty states that do not guess why they are empty
column5:
Spike A's most useful finding: a denied read is indistinguishable from no data, and there is no permission-denied branch to write. The spike's own empty state got this wrong in front of its author - it read 40 workouts and then printed "either there is nothing recorded, or read access was declined". Both halves were false.

Acceptance criteria
* Every data surface has a designed empty state whose wording covers both causes without claiming either
* "No daily totals for this type" and stop - no speculation about permissions
* Repositories return empty, never throw, when there is no data

column2: Read workouts passively, build no workout UI
column5:
ADR 0009. Workouts give the ranking engine training signal without any workout UI, which is exactly how the v1 scope stays sane.

Acceptance criteria
* workout_count lands in health_samples
* No workout screen, no workout logging, nothing in the tab bar

column2: Sub On screen: four routes, the Squad and the Bench
column4: P1-F Sub On: food logging, four routes
column5:
design/redesign/screens/3-sub-on.png. Most people rotate through roughly thirty distinct foods; surfacing frequent (The Squad) and recent (On the Bench) first makes search feel dramatically faster than the incumbents' without any clever algorithm.

Acceptance criteria
* Four routes visible: manual, search, barcode, photo
* The Squad (frequent) and On the Bench (recent) populated from the user's own history
* First Half / Second Half meal periods assign correctly across a date boundary

column2: Path 0: manual entry
column4: P1-F Sub On: food logging, four routes
column5:
The fourth route in the redesign, and the one that starts the 21-day clock. It works offline by construction and depends on nothing external.

Acceptance criteria
* Log a food by name, grams and macros with no network
* entry_method = manual
* Fast enough to use daily without irritation - this is the path that will carry the first week

column2: Path 1: text search against the mirrored database
column4: P1-F Sub On: food logging, four routes
column5:
Brief SS1.3. Search hits your own Postgres, never a third-party API on a keystroke.

Acceptance criteria
* Debounced query against the tsvector index; results feel instant
* Recent and frequent foods surface above raw search results
* Works with no signal against a local cache of the user's own food set
* entry_method = search

column2: Path 2: barcode via VisionKit DataScannerViewController
column4: P1-F Sub On: food logging, four routes
column5:
"The fastest logging path that exists for packaged food and it is close to free to implement. Prioritise it." Roughly twenty lines - do not hand-roll AVFoundation.

Acceptance criteria
* Scan resolves against the mirrored Open Food Facts data
* Unknown barcode falls back to manual search rather than dead-ending, and offers to save as a custom food
* entry_method = barcode

column2: Path 3: photo estimate via a Supabase Edge Function
column4: P1-F Sub On: food logging, four routes
column5:
Capture or pick, downscale to ~1024 px on the longest edge before upload (materially cuts cost and latency, accuracy barely moves), upload to Storage, Edge Function calls the vision model with a structured-output prompt, returns items with ranges and a confidence level.

Never call the AI API from the app - keys in a client binary are extractable in minutes.

Acceptance criteria
* End-to-end round trip on a real photo, on a real device
* Provider sits behind an interface (ADR 0010), so swapping arms costs nothing
* Structured output validated before it reaches the UI; a malformed response degrades to manual entry
* Measured latency recorded (the spike saw 1.9-3.1 s)

column2: Under Review: the mandatory confirm-and-correct screen
column4: P1-F Sub On: food logging, four routes
column5:
design/redesign/screens/4-under-review.png. Nothing logs until the user gives the decision. Trained dietitians misestimate by 20-30% and the models do worse; owning that loudly is better product design than pretending otherwise.

Acceptance criteria
* No estimate can reach food_logs without an explicit confirmation
* Range and confidence are both visible; the range renders as figure plus tolerance, never two numbers joined by a dash
* Correction is one tap
* was_corrected and correction_delta written to photo_estimates on every pass - that dataset is how the prompt improves later

column2: Per-user daily photo cap in the Edge Function
column4: P1-F Sub On: food logging, four routes
column5:
SS10: add the cap before you hand the app to anyone, not after a surprise bill. Measured cost is $0.000862/image, so this is an abuse control rather than a cost control - 20-30 photos/day is generous enough that no honest user reaches it while still bounding a runaway client loop.

Acceptance criteria
* Cap enforced server-side, not in the client
* Hitting it produces calm copy and an intact manual path, not an error

column2: Keep the photo alongside the confirmed values
column4: P1-F Sub On: food logging, four routes
column5:
Phase 0 folded the photo-accuracy benchmark into Phase 1 (ADR 0010) on one condition: that Phase 1's logging keeps the photo alongside the confirmed values, so the 21 days produce the dataset instead of a separate evening's collection.

Acceptance criteria
* storage_path, model_output, confidence and the user's confirmed values all persist together
* The set is exportable in a shape spikes/vision-accuracy can score

column2: Weight entry: manual plus HealthKit
column5:
Smart scales write to HealthKit automatically; manual entry covers everyone else.

Acceptance criteria
* Both sources land in weight_logs with source set correctly
* No duplicate when the same reading arrives both ways
* Works offline

column2: 7-day EWMA trend in Swift Charts
column5:
Brief SS1.5: never display raw daily weight. Daily weight is mostly water, glycogen and gut content; showing it raw produces a jagged line that makes a genuinely successful week look like failure, and it is one of the main reasons people abandon weight-loss apps in the first fortnight.

Acceptance criteria
* 7-day exponentially weighted moving average, rendered with Swift Charts
* Raw daily values are never the primary series
* Trend is correct across gaps in the data

column2: One-point and no-point trend states
column5:
Measured in Spike A: bodyweight read 120.00 kg from a single same-day entry, so the 30-day trend had exactly one point. Nothing was wrong - there was simply no back-history. The trend view needs "one data point" as a real designed state, not a sparse-data edge case.

Acceptance criteria
* Zero points, one point and two points each render deliberately
* Wording does not speculate about why data is missing (see the HealthKit empty-state ticket)

column2: Pace against the rate chosen at onboarding
column5:
design/redesign/screens/5-the-run.png - weight and trend against the pace you chose.

Acceptance criteria
* Target pace line derived from the S3-filtered rate on the profile
* Being ahead of pace is not celebrated - the engine caps rate of loss for safety and celebration of speed would fight it (PRODUCT.md, S3)
* Being behind pace uses copy-deck wording, never punishment framing

column2: Band and remaining, on the pitch
column5:
design/redesign/screens/2-matchday.png. The daily driver: band, pitch, team sheet.

Acceptance criteria
* Remaining renders as a figure plus tolerance
* Going over the band uses no error colour - the token set deliberately has none for this, and critical is destructive-confirm only
* Real evidence values from PRODUCT.md during development, never lorem or round numbers

column2: Macro split
column5:
Acceptance criteria
* Protein / carbs / fat from the day's logs
* Renders sensibly at zero logs, one log and twenty

column2: Weight sparkline on Matchday
column5:
The EWMA series from The Run, compressed to a glance.

Acceptance criteria
* Shares the trend calculation with The Run - one implementation, not two
* Degrades to the one-point state

column2: Form: the 7-day consistency ring
column5:
Form is the redesign's name for 7-day consistency. Consistency is 0.50 of the eventual score, so this is the surface the whole thesis leans on.

Acceptance criteria
* A missed day renders empty, never crossed out; no streak-loss animation (S5)
* No confetti or speed-rewarding celebration anywhere (PRODUCT.md)
* The ring is legible without colour alone

column2: Division badge placeholder for Phase 2
column5:
Brief SS1.6 asks for a placeholder where the tier badge sits in Phase 2.

Acceptance criteria
* A reserved, honest placeholder - no invented tier, no sample rank, no other user's name or number anywhere in v1

column2: Outbox and the sync service
column5:
ADR 0005. An outbox table holds pending mutations; a sync service drains it when connectivity returns. Last-write-wins on server timestamps for v1 - document the limitation rather than building CRDTs.

Acceptance criteria
* Every mutation enqueues to sync_outbox with entity, operation, payload and attempts
* Drain is idempotent; a replayed payload does not duplicate a row
* Backoff on repeated failure; attempts is honoured rather than looping
* The last-write-wins limitation is written down where a future reader will find it

column2: Airplane-mode verification
column5:
Phase 1 exit criterion: "Outbox sync verified by using the app in airplane mode."

Acceptance criteria
* A full day logged in airplane mode: food, weight, corrections
* Nothing blocks on the network; no spinner waits on a request
* Everything reconciles correctly on reconnect, in order, with no duplicates and no loss
* Gyms and restaurant basements have no signal - this is the scenario, not a synthetic one

column2: Start the 21-day clock
column5:
The clock cannot start until the app can be used daily on the real device. The minimum set is: onboarding produces a band, manual entry works, weight entry works, and it all persists locally.

Everything else in the phase - barcode, photo, background HealthKit delivery, the Matchday polish - can land while the 21 days run, provided a change never breaks a day's logging.

Acceptance criteria
* Day 0 date recorded on this ticket
* Dev build installed on the phone and surviving a rebuild without wiping the local store

column2: Log 21 consecutive days of real data
column5:
Non-negotiable, and the phase's actual purpose. Your own three weeks of logs are the test set for the entire crown jewel of this project - Phase 2 cannot design a fair ranking system without them.

Acceptance criteria
* 21 consecutive days, real food, real weight, no synthetic backfill
* A broken day breaks the streak - be honest about it in the tracker rather than quietly ticking it (repo convention)
* Data survives every app update shipped during the window

column2: Photo-accuracy benchmark from the 21 days
column5:
Moved out of Phase 0's exit criteria and folded into Phase 1 (ADR 0010): it is a benchmark, not a spike - it calibrates a feature rather than killing one. The meals arrive from real use.

Acceptance criteria
* At least 20 photo-logged meals with the model's estimate and the confirmed value both retained
* Scored through spikes/vision-accuracy and written into docs/phase-0/07-spike-findings.md
* No invented baseline before the data exists - "do not invent one" (PRODUCT.md)

column2: Bug intake from daily use
column5:
Everything found while actually using the app lands here and gets triaged, rather than being fixed in place and forgotten.

Acceptance criteria
* A running list, triaged weekly into fix-now / fix-in-phase-2 / won't-fix
* Anything that breaks a day's logging is fix-now by definition

column2: EXIT: 21 consecutive days of real data logged
column5: Non-negotiable. This is the phase's actual purpose. Closed by the dogfood epic.

column2: EXIT: all four logging routes work, offline included
column5: Brief says three paths; the redesign adds manual as a fourth. Offline is part of the criterion, not a follow-up.

column2: EXIT: HealthKit incremental sync with a persisted anchor
column5: Proven the way Spike A proved it: a cold launch after a sync reads approximately nothing.
